# `bank-rule` commands

## `bank-rule accept`

Accept a suggested (learned) bank rule: it becomes active and proposes for its payee's lines. Example: {"rule": "01J..."}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | bank-feed |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bank-rule.accept` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow bank-rule accept "Coffee Bean (learned)" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Yes, always" --json`

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:


## `bank-rule apply`

Read the rules over the waiting lines again: each line's rule proposal becomes the first rule that fits now (decided lines are never touched; nothing is added or ignored). With rule, only the lines that rule gains or loses. --dry-run lists what would change. Example: {"rule": "Shell fuel"}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | bank-feed |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bank-rule.apply` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow bank-rule apply --rule "Shell fuel" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Propose the new rule for waiting lines" --dry-run --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "bank-rule apply", "input": {"rule": "Shell fuel"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rule` | `--rule` | string \| null | no | yes | null | One rule (by id or name); omitted, every active rule in order. |
| `account` | `--account` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Only this account's waiting lines. |
| `limit` | `--limit` | integer | no | no | 1000 | Most waiting lines to read.; minimum 1; maximum 20000 |

## `bank-rule create`

Write a bank rule: the lines it fits (an account or every feed account, money in, out or any, and conditions that all hold: payee, payee_key, memo or number contains, starts_with or equals; amount equals or between) and what it proposes: categorise (payee, category account, class, memo), transfer (to an account) or ignore (with a reason). Rules are tried by priority (lower first; a written rule is 100, a learned one 1000), then a rule for the line's own account first, then specificity; the first that fits wins and the line shows it. A rule only proposes: auto_add (or an ignore rule) is a request that acts only once a holder of automate.bank-rule makes it live with `bank-rule update --live`. 'Always put Shell under Fuel' means create a proposal-only rule, using payee contains SHELL so descriptions with store numbers or other suffixes still fit; use equals only when the owner asks for an exact description. Then bank-rule apply --dry-run to show waiting lines it fits; apply to refresh their proposals. Report that it does not post unattended. Do not enable auto-add from that wording alone. Example: {"name": "Shell fuel", "account": "Checking", "direction": "out", "conditions": [{"field": "payee", "op": "contains", "value": "SHELL"}], "payee": "Shell", "category": "Fuel"}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | bank-feed |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bank-rule.create` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow bank-rule create --name "Shell fuel" --account Checking --direction out --conditions '[{"field": "payee", "op": "contains", "value": "SHELL"}]' --payee "Central Supply" --category "Vehicle Expense" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Always put Shell under fuel" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "bank-rule create", "input": {"name": "Shell fuel", "account": "Checking", "direction": "out", "conditions": [{"field": "payee", "op": "contains", "value": "SHELL"}], "payee": "Central Supply", "category": "Vehicle Expense"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `account` | `--account` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The bank or card account whose lines it fits; omitted or null, every feed account. |
| `direction` | `--direction` | literal["in", "out", "any"] \| null | no | yes | null | in (money in), out (money out) or any; default any. |
| `conditions[].field` | inside `--conditions` JSON array | literal["payee", "payee_key", "memo", "number", "amount"] | yes | no | — | What is tested: the bank's payee text, payee_key (the payee as Bookflow reads it: letters only, store and reference numbers, dates and processor words dropped), memo, number, or amount (the size of the line, in either direction). |
| `conditions[].op` | inside `--conditions` JSON array | literal["contains", "starts_with", "equals", "between"] | yes | no | — | contains, starts_with or equals (text, case-folded with spaces collapsed; payee_key takes equals); between (amount only, value to value_to inclusive). No regular expressions. |
| `conditions[].value` | inside `--conditions` JSON array | string | yes | no | — | The text, or an amount such as 45.00.; minimum length 1; maximum length 200 |
| `conditions[].value_to` | inside `--conditions` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | between: the upper amount. |
| `action` | `--action` | literal["categorise", "transfer", "ignore"] \| null | no | yes | null | categorise (propose a payee, account, class and memo; the default), transfer (propose a transfer to transfer_to) or ignore (propose setting the line aside with ignore_reason). |
| `payee` | `--payee` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Categorise: who the line is from or to, an existing name (or its id) on the payee_type list; shown on the line and used when it is added. |
| `payee_type` | `--payee-type` | literal["customer", "vendor", "employee", "other_name"] \| null | no | yes | null | The list the payee is on; default vendor. |
| `category` | `--category` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Categorise: the account a line goes to when added (an expense or income account...). |
| `class_id` | `--class-id` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Categorise: the class an added line takes. |
| `memo` | `--memo` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Categorise: the memo; default the bank's text. |
| `transfer_to` | `--transfer-to` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Transfer: the other account. |
| `ignore_reason` | `--ignore-reason` | literal["already_entered", "not_ours", "duplicate", "other"] \| null | no | yes | null | Ignore: why (default other). |
| `auto_add` | `--auto-add` | boolean \| null | no | yes | null | Categorise: ask to add matching lines unattended at each import. A request: it acts only once a holder of automate.bank-rule makes the rule live (`bank-rule update --live`), and then under that holder's authority. |
| `priority` | `--priority` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | Lower is tried first; default 100 (a learned rule is 1000, so a written rule beats it). |
| `name` | `--name` | string | yes | no | — | A name to know it by, unique.; minimum length 1; maximum length 200 |

## `bank-rule update`

Change a bank rule, make an auto-add or ignore rule live, or pause one (live false). Making it live needs automate.bank-rule and one check of its exact details: --dry-run returns check (what it will do, the waiting lines it fits now, a fingerprint); pass the fingerprint as confirm. It then acts at each later import under your authority. A change to what a live rule does by anyone without automate.bank-rule returns it to draft; by a holder it stays live under them only with the new check confirmed. A learned rule you change is kept when its import is reversed. Example: {"rule": "Shell fuel", "live": true, "confirm": "<fingerprint>"}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | bank-feed |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bank-rule.update` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow bank-rule update "Shell fuel" --live --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Add Shell lines unattended" --dry-run --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "bank-rule update", "input": {"rule": "Shell fuel", "live": true}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `account` | `--account` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The bank or card account whose lines it fits; omitted or null, every feed account. |
| `direction` | `--direction` | literal["in", "out", "any"] \| null | no | yes | null | in (money in), out (money out) or any; default any. |
| `conditions[].field` | inside `--conditions` JSON array | literal["payee", "payee_key", "memo", "number", "amount"] | yes | no | — | What is tested: the bank's payee text, payee_key (the payee as Bookflow reads it: letters only, store and reference numbers, dates and processor words dropped), memo, number, or amount (the size of the line, in either direction). |
| `conditions[].op` | inside `--conditions` JSON array | literal["contains", "starts_with", "equals", "between"] | yes | no | — | contains, starts_with or equals (text, case-folded with spaces collapsed; payee_key takes equals); between (amount only, value to value_to inclusive). No regular expressions. |
| `conditions[].value` | inside `--conditions` JSON array | string | yes | no | — | The text, or an amount such as 45.00.; minimum length 1; maximum length 200 |
| `conditions[].value_to` | inside `--conditions` JSON array | string \| null | no | yes | null | between: the upper amount. |
| `action` | `--action` | literal["categorise", "transfer", "ignore"] \| null | no | yes | null | categorise (propose a payee, account, class and memo; the default), transfer (propose a transfer to transfer_to) or ignore (propose setting the line aside with ignore_reason). |
| `payee` | `--payee` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Categorise: who the line is from or to, an existing name (or its id) on the payee_type list; shown on the line and used when it is added. |
| `payee_type` | `--payee-type` | literal["customer", "vendor", "employee", "other_name"] \| null | no | yes | null | The list the payee is on; default vendor. |
| `category` | `--category` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Categorise: the account a line goes to when added (an expense or income account...). |
| `class_id` | `--class-id` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Categorise: the class an added line takes. |
| `memo` | `--memo` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Categorise: the memo; default the bank's text. |
| `transfer_to` | `--transfer-to` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Transfer: the other account. |
| `ignore_reason` | `--ignore-reason` | literal["already_entered", "not_ours", "duplicate", "other"] \| null | no | yes | null | Ignore: why (default other). |
| `auto_add` | `--auto-add` | boolean \| null | no | yes | null | Categorise: ask to add matching lines unattended at each import. A request: it acts only once a holder of automate.bank-rule makes the rule live (`bank-rule update --live`), and then under that holder's authority. |
| `priority` | `--priority` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | Lower is tried first; default 100 (a learned rule is 1000, so a written rule beats it). |
| `rule` | `RULE` | string | yes | no | — | The rule, by id or name.; minimum length 1; maximum length 200 |
| `name` | `--name` | string \| null | no | yes | null | A new name. |
| `status` | `--status` | literal["active", "disabled"] \| null | no | yes | null | active fits lines again; disabled stops it fitting any (`bank-rule deactivate`). |
| `live` | `--live` | boolean \| null | no | yes | null | true: make this auto-add or ignore rule act on its own at each import, under your authority (needs automate.bank-rule). --dry-run shows the check (what it will do and the waiting lines it fits now) and its fingerprint; pass that as confirm. |
| `confirm` | `--confirm` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The check's fingerprint from a dry run: needed to make a rule live, and for a holder's change to keep a live rule live (without it, the change returns the rule to draft). |
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | Refused if the rule changed since. |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate and preview without writing. |
| `--reason TEXT` | Short reason for the write. |
| `--source-ref TEXT` | Identifier of the source that triggered the write. |
| `--interactive` | Prompt for input fields not supplied as arguments or options. |
| `--directive TEXT` | Standing-instruction code or id cited by the write. |
| `--idempotency-key TEXT` | Retry-safe key for this create command. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/bank-rule.update`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |
| `X-Bookflow-Source-Ref` | optional | Identifier of the source that triggered the write |
| `X-Bookflow-Directive` | conditional | Active directive code or id; alternative to reason for an agent or system write |
| `Idempotency-Key` | optional | Retry-safe key for this create command |

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_AMOUNT_PRECISION` | The amount has more decimal places than the currency allows. |
| `E_COMPANY_AMBIGUOUS` | More than one company matches; use the id or Organization/Company. |
| `E_COMPANY_NOT_FOUND` | No such company. |
| `E_CONFIG_INVALID` | The configuration file could not be read. |
| `E_CONTEXT_IN_INPUT` | Input contains a context field. |
| `E_DB_BUSY` | Another Bookflow command is running on this data root. |
| `E_DIRECTIVE_INACTIVE` | That directive has been deactivated. |
| `E_DIRECTIVE_NOT_FOUND` | No such directive. |
| `E_FEATURE_DISABLED` | This feature is not enabled for the company. |
| `E_FS_UNKNOWN` | The filesystem type of the path could not be determined. |
| `E_GUARD_REFUSED` | Bookflow's own safety check in the database refused this write, so nothing was saved. This is a Bookflow bug, not a problem with your input or your disk: please report it with this error's details and request id. |
| `E_IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH` | That idempotency key was used for a different command or input. |
| `E_INTERNAL` | Internal failure. |
| `E_IO` | A filesystem operation failed. |
| `E_MIGRATION_FAILED` | A schema migration failed; the database was backed up first and is unchanged. |
| `E_NAME_TAKEN` | That display name is already used. |
| `E_NETWORK_SHARE` | The path is on a network filesystem, which Bookflow refuses to use. |
| `E_NOT_INITIALIZED` | The data root is not initialized; run `bookflow init`. |
| `E_NO_ACTOR` | This login is not mapped to a Bookflow user. |
| `E_ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND` | No such organization. |
| `E_PARTIAL_WRITE` | The authoritative write committed, but a secondary update remains incomplete. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The acting user may not run this command here. |
| `E_REASON_REQUIRED` | This write needs a reason: a short phrase naming what triggered it (--reason on the CLI, a top-level reason on MCP, the X-Bookflow-Reason header on HTTP). |
| `E_RECORD_NOT_FOUND` | No such record. |
| `E_SCHEMA_BEHIND` | The database schema is behind this version of Bookflow; run `bookflow upgrade`. |
| `E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN` | The database schema revision is not known to this version of Bookflow; upgrade Bookflow. |
| `E_UNAUTHENTICATED` | No valid credential: log in, or send a bearer token. |
